doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Joe's loyalty to jazz while others cross over
summary: Joe never moved to rock, pop or country; she compares Harry Connick and Barry Manilow's big band album.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Have you noticed over the years, has Joe been affected by changes in the music business more than, or does he kind of have his own style?
No, he’s never changed his belief in what he wants to do. I mean he would never go to rock ‘n roll or pop music or country & western.
Right because some people have tried it.

Well people are trying it and I suppose being very successful. One example would be Harry Connick, who used to sing big band stuff and do nice things. He’s now gone to pop and noise and rock ‘n roll and stuff which is probably making him more money, but it’s deserting the cause.
It seemed like he was pretty successful to me.
And someone who has sort of come back is Barry Manilow, who has done a wonderful big band album.
Yes. So it will never die but it probably won’t ever be the same, the big band business.
